npcs.greeting: The same hands made every version of your set. Leave the piece with me and take the one that suits how you fight now. No charge. Keepers do not sell.

npcs.name: Thane Morgrim Onyxhand
npcs.greeting:
You came down through the Dry Deep. We don't get many who do.

I'm Morgrim. I run the working, which means the mine, the forges and the gate. Trade's welcome and the shops are on the Row behind you. If you're looking for work as well, talk to Captain Yrsa at the gate. She always has more trouble than guards.

npcs.name: Forgemaster Garrun Slagborn
npcs.greeting:
I teach mining and smithing, and I teach them together. I've no use for a smith who can't tell good ore from bad.

Show me what you already know and we'll start from there.

npcs.name: Gate-Captain Yrsa Stonebar
npcs.greeting:
The Thane says the gate opens for trade, so it opens for you. I'd still like to know your business before you go back out.

There are three things to watch for out there. The hive's to the south-east. The mushroom wood is south-west, and it's worse than it looks. North-east are the old diggings, and the people in them used to live here. Don't expect a welcome.

npcs.name: Gate-Guard Dunmar
npcs.greeting: Knock the sand off your boots before you go up the Row, would you? Hulda found grit in her quench last week and we all heard about it.

npcs.name: Gate-Guard Oda
npcs.greeting: Six years I've stood on this gate. I've seen the hive come right up to the towers twice. Both times they turned round at the braziers, so we keep the braziers lit.

npcs.name: Sentry Rurik Boltwright
npcs.greeting:
Quiet a moment.

...No. Thought I heard digging. The hive tunnels under the wall sometimes, so I spend most of my watch with an ear to the rock. You get so you can tell them from our own miners.

npcs.name: Vault-Keeper Aldis Greylock
npcs.greeting:
Every bar poured in Onyxhollow gets weighed and written down here. I have the books going back to the first shaft.

Some of the names in the early ones belong to people who were put out of the gate. The Thane wanted them struck from the record. I told him the weights were still true, and he let it go.

npcs.name: Ashkeeper Torvald
npcs.greeting:
This fire was lit from the first furnace we built, and it hasn't gone out since. Keeping it fed is my whole job.

You're welcome to warm your hands. Half the town does on their way to shift.

npcs.name: Stoker Hald Cinderlung
npcs.greeting:
The furnace takes a cart of coal a shift, and I'm the one who shovels it.

Garrun says the heat is where the craft is. He's probably right, but I notice he says it from the other side of the yard.

npcs.name: Loremaster Ingrid Pagewright
npcs.greeting:
Have you seen the walls out on the Strand? There are tide marks on them, high up. That was a sea once, with a shoreline, and somebody must have lived on it.

I'd like to find out who. The Thane thinks it's a waste of lamp oil, so I mostly ask travellers. If you come across anything out there that looks made rather than grown, I'd be glad to hear about it.

npcs.name: Geomancer Vigdis Stonesong
npcs.greeting:
You walked through the caves above us to get here, the dry ones with the holes up to the desert. That's our roof, and it's a lot thinner than people here like to think about.

I listen to it for the Thane. It's holding, for now. I'd be happier if things stopped eating the pillars.

npcs.name: Lookout Hervi Longstair
npcs.greeting:
You made it down. Sit a minute if you need to, it's a long stair.

I'm posted here to see who comes down and send them on to the gate. Follow the slag road south-east and keep to it. You'll see the braziers. Onyxhollow's at the end, between the two towers.

npcs.name: Noor Haddad
npcs.greeting:
Oh, hello. Sorry, I don't get many people coming past.

I'm a geologist. I was one before all this, in Amman, and it turns out the job still exists if you don't mind who you work for. The surveyors up at Fourth Peg told me about the caves and I kept going down. I've been camped here about a month. The dwarves think I'm odd but they sell me bread.

npcs.name: Brannoc
npcs.greeting:
I'm allowed as far as this brazier. Yrsa lets me sit here as long as I don't go near the gate.

I lived in there for forty years. I was put out with the rest of my shift and I've been in the old diggings since. If you're going into town, don't tell them you spoke to me. It won't help you.

npcs.name: Wind-Rider Tazzi Updraft
npcs.greeting:
Need a lift out? It's a long climb otherwise.

I fly from the platform. The birds like it down here, there's water and it's out of the wind. Getting them to leave again is the hard part. I can take you to Steamwheedle Port or anywhere beyond it you've already been.

npcs.name: Dr. Imani Mwangi
npcs.greeting:
If you're hurt, sit down on the crate and I'll have a look.

I ran the clinic on the Likoni ferry in Mombasa for eleven years. Three years ago the ferry docked at a pier that hadn't been there that morning, and I've been treating dwarves and goblins ever since. Most of what I see here is burns.

npcs.name: Shipwright Rozz Keelhaul
npcs.greeting:
I build the barges that carry ore round the island.

They gave me this beach, a saw pit and a crew of four. I've launched six hulls since spring and I've only got two left. Something out in the shallows keeps sinking them.

npcs.name: Teodora Vasquez
npcs.greeting:
Please watch where you step. Half of what's growing here hasn't been named yet.

I taught botany at the university in Quito before I came through. The Ashclaim pays me to tell them which plants on this island are worth money. Nothing here is in any of my books.

npcs.name: Foreman Brakka Sootmantle
npcs.greeting:
This is the Ashclaim Works. The smelter behind me is the only thing on the island making money right now.

I've got sixty people working here. The ground shakes twice a day and the Cinder Flats are full of fire elementals, so keeping all sixty of them alive takes most of my time.

npcs.name: Enginewright Tobble Vantz
npcs.greeting:
I keep the pump engine and the winding gear at the mine head running.

The air off the vents eats brass in a month and iron in a season, so I spend most of my time rebuilding things I've already built.

npcs.name: Doorwarden Kettil Grimstead
npcs.greeting:
That opening goes down into the Emberdeep. I'm here to tell people what's down there before they go in.

There's a lake of molten rock with islands of cooled stone in it, and everything living down there came out of the lake. The Thane's people sealed this door a long time ago. It broke open three years ago.

npcs.name: Coast-Surveyor Mizzi Dredgeline
npcs.greeting:
I'm charting this coast for a harbour, and I've lost two boats doing it.

The wrecks along this shore are older than the Ashclaim. Somebody was sailing here long before the goblins came, and the naga have moved into what's left of their ships.

npcs.name: Scout Varga Cinderstep
npcs.greeting:
Stay on the dark ground out here. The pale crust is thin and there's steam under it.

I walk the Cinder Flats for the Foreman and mark where the vents have moved, so the ore carts know which way is safe. They move most weeks.

npcs.name: Assayer Ruddi Halfweight
npcs.greeting:
I weigh and test every load of ore that comes out of the mine.

The dwarves get paid by what I weigh, so a lot of them think I'm cheating them. I'm not, and I'm the reason the goblins aren't either.

npcs.name: Blaster Orrin Slowmatch
npcs.greeting:
I set the blasting charges at the mine head. Please don't smoke near the red shed.

Blasting inside a volcano takes a lot of care. The last blaster here lost both his hands.

npcs.name: Dr. Kenji Arakawa
npcs.greeting:
I watch the volcano for the Ashclaim and tell them when it's dangerous.

I worked at the observatory in Kagoshima for twenty years, watching Sakurajima. Three years ago I walked out of the building and the bay was gone. This mountain doesn't behave like any volcano I've studied.

npcs.name: Harbourmaster Skezz Mooringline
npcs.greeting:
I run the berths. Every boat that ties up here pays a fee.

I've lost four barges between here and the landing this season, and the Underwriter wants to know why. So do I.

npcs.name: Deedkeeper Thora Runebrand
npcs.greeting:
I keep the rolls of Khaz Varun, the records of every birth, oath and debt from before the city went dark.

The Thane's claim depends on these rolls, so I keep the key on a cord round my neck.

npcs.name: Adjuster Priya Raman
npcs.greeting:
I assess losses for the Underwriter. When a barge sinks, I work out whether it was bad luck or bad seamanship.

I did the same job for a marine insurer in Singapore. Three years ago I was inspecting a container ship when the harbour changed around it. The goblins understand insurance better than anyone I worked with there.

npcs.name: Battlemaster Ingra Coalbeard
npcs.greeting:
I train fighters of every kind, and I don't much care which kind you are.

The Thane brought me over to teach his own people before they went into the hall. Most of them have gone in now, so I've got time for anyone who can pay. Show me what you can do and I'll show you what comes next.

npcs.name: Forgemaster Ulfa Hammerdeep
npcs.greeting:
If you want to mine Khaz Varun's iron or work it, I can teach you both.

The ore on this island is better than anything on the mainland, and dark iron's the best of it. It's also the fussiest metal you'll ever put in a fire, so learn it from someone who's ruined plenty of it.

npcs.name: Herbalist Zinnia Sporewick
npcs.greeting:
I can teach you which plants on this island are worth picking and what to do with them once you've got them.

The Green Belt's full of things the mainland's never seen. Half of them will heal you and the other half will put you in Dr. Mwangi's tent, so it's worth paying someone to tell you which half is which.

npcs.name: Tanner Brog Ashpelt
npcs.greeting:
I work hides, leather and cloth, and I cook, because nobody else on this wharf will do it properly. I'll teach you to fish for the pot as well.

A basilisk hide off the Cinder Flats makes the best leather I've ever handled. I'll teach you to skin it, cure it and stitch it, and I'll teach you what to do with the meat while you're at it.

npcs.name: Woodwright Kibble Sawtooth
npcs.greeting:
I can teach you to cut timber and work it, and on this island that mostly means bloodwood and felbark.

The jungle wood's too green for hulls, so I use it for everything else. If you want to know which trees are worth felling, I've felled most of the wrong ones already.

npcs.name: Tinker Fezzik Coilspring
npcs.greeting:
I teach engineering, and I'll tell you now that the vents on this island will try to eat everything you build.

I keep the town's pumps running when Tobble at the Works can spare me a gasket. If you want to learn how to build something that lasts out here, I'm the one to ask.

npcs.name: Artifact Keeper Hilde Ironveil
npcs.greeting:
I can change a set piece you're wearing into the version that suits the way you fight now, and I don't charge for it.

If you've brought a token up from the old city or out of the Emberdeep, I'll turn that into a piece for you as well. The Keepers sent me here because this is where the tokens are being found.

npcs.name: Sentry Garrick Hale
npcs.greeting: Keep walking. The militia hasn't decided whether you're worth the arrows yet.

npcs.name: Sentry Ivy Coombs
npcs.greeting: One step past this post and we stop being polite. We've only just started being polite.

npcs.name: Militia Captain Ros Callard
npcs.greeting: Southshore stands because people like me stand at its gate. Remember that if you're thinking of trying it.

npcs.name: Dockmaster Ewan Pryce
npcs.greeting: Every crate on this quay gets counted twice. If one goes missing, I'll know whose boots were nearest.

npcs.name: Netmender Rose Abernathy
npcs.greeting: My husband sailed with the Lordaeron fleet and never came home. Mind the nets, they're all I've got left of him.

npcs.name: Brother Aldous Venn
npcs.greeting: The Light doesn't ask what you are. The people of this town do. I'm sorry for that, I really am.

npcs.name: Farmer Tom Holloway
npcs.greeting: Turnips, cabbages and no trouble. That's all I'm asking of this season, and I'm not getting the last one.

npcs.name: Pip Corwin
npcs.greeting: Are you really an orc? My mum says orcs eat people. You don't look very hungry.

npcs.name: Wharf-Boss Grizzle
npcs.greeting: Everything that comes off a ship comes past me. I've got a list. You're not on it yet.

npcs.name: Gunner Spark
npcs.greeting: Bloodsail sails come round that point about once a week. I'm the reason they keep going.

npcs.name: Lucky Fen
npcs.greeting: Three to one the Crimson Gull doesn't make Ratchet. Want in? Course you do.

npcs.name: Old Tansy
npcs.greeting: Hold that end. No, the other end. You've never held a net before, have you.

npcs.name: Deckhand Mox
npcs.greeting: Unload, load, unload. The tide doesn't take a day off, so neither do I.

npcs.name: Velvet Pike
npcs.greeting: I'm not here. You didn't see me. And if you did, you saw somebody taller.

npcs.name: Deathguard Pell
npcs.greeting: Marl has the days at the Shadowfang gate. I have the nights. The nights are louder.

npcs.name: Tamsin Hale
npcs.greeting: I write down what the magister says, and then I write down what he meant.

npcs.name: Arch Druid Aelyra Moonbough
npcs.greeting: Welcome to the Sanctuary. Everyone here came for a different reason, and we've stopped asking which.

npcs.name: Captain Saranis Duskwhisper
npcs.greeting: The Fel Line's north of the barricade. We hold it, and every week it's a little further north than it was.

npcs.name: Elder Grumhall Oakpelt
npcs.greeting: The Timbermaw remember when the Deadwood were our cousins. We'd like to remember it with them again.

npcs.name: Old Thornbark
npcs.greeting: I was standing here before the glade was cleansed. I'd like to still be standing here after.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Nelanthe Softbough
npcs.greeting: There's a bed and a hot meal, and nobody will ask you to plant anything until morning.

npcs.name: Faelin Skybough
npcs.greeting: The hippogryphs fly anywhere you've been. They won't go near the Fel Line, and neither should you without a reason.

npcs.name: Dr. Nkechi Adeyemi
npcs.greeting: I was an emergency doctor in Lagos. The wounds here are stranger, but the work's the same. Sit down if you're bleeding.

npcs.name: Tomasz Wolny
npcs.greeting: I built houses outside Kraków. Now I build barricades, and the Sentinels tell me I'm slow. I tell them it's called doing it properly.

npcs.name: Yuki Hashimoto
npcs.greeting: I'm cataloguing everything that grows back. Three years ago I didn't know any of these plants existed, and now I know more of them than I know people here.

npcs.name: Ana Lúcia Ferreira
npcs.greeting: First time in the Sanctuary? The inn's on your left, the roost's past it, and the Arch Druid's at the well if you want to be useful.

npcs.name: Barkwarden Elm
npcs.greeting: The Sentinels stand on the line, and so do I. The difference is that they talk more.

npcs.name: Druid Talenwe Rootsong
npcs.greeting: I'll teach you what grows on cleansed ground and what to make of it. Most of it heals. The rest you'll want to keep away from the soup.

npcs.name: Captain Elanya Swiftbrook
npcs.greeting: This is as far north as the Reclamation holds. We're here so the Sanctuary knows what's coming before it comes.

npcs.name: Druid Arathel Greenvale
npcs.greeting: The ground inside the stakes is clean because I clean it every morning. Don't bring anything green and glowing back with you.

npcs.name: Scout Barrowpaw
npcs.greeting: Felpaw was my cousins' village. I still know every path in and out of it, and I'll tell you which ones they're watching.

npcs.name: Marcus Oyelaran
npcs.greeting: I was a paramedic in Toronto. Up here it's burns, bites and things I don't have names for yet. If it's spreading, show me now and not later.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Thornclaw
npcs.greeting: The tunnel behind me is the Timbermaw's road through the mountain. The Elders have opened it to anyone who comes in peace, so mind your manners up there.

npcs.name: Sentinel Ilthara Swiftleaf
npcs.greeting: Captain Saranis sent two of us down with a lantern. It isn't much of a garrison, but the road's watched again. The Sanctuary's north, then east at the fork.

npcs.name: Sentinel Aeris Moonvale
npcs.greeting: I keep the lantern lit and my eyes on the road. Mostly it's travellers from Ashenvale. Every so often it's something worse coming down from the north.

npcs.name: Elder Muhana Windhoof
npcs.greeting: Sun Rock used to be a quiet place to sit and watch the mountain. Now half of Thunder Bluff sleeps on it, and I'm the one they come to when something goes wrong.

npcs.name: Spiritwalker Tohana
npcs.greeting: The spirits here are restless. They were restless before the mountain blew, and it hasn't helped.

npcs.name: Watch Captain Ahrok Stonemane
npcs.greeting: From this tower you can see the whole Blowdown. You can also see the Venture Co. carting it away, which I'd rather not watch.

npcs.name: Kuna Ashhorn
npcs.greeting: That's Mulgore out there. You can see where the daylight stops. I watch it so the people who came from there don't have to.

npcs.name: Halona Stillwater
npcs.greeting: We carried out what we could. It turned out to be less than we thought, and more than some people managed.

npcs.name: Tavo Longrun
npcs.greeting: I hunted Mulgore my whole life. I know every trail in it. I'm not going back to see what's walking them now.

npcs.name: Envoy Garnak
npcs.greeting: Orgrimmar sent me to make sure Sun Rock holds. The Grimtotem think it won't. I'd like to prove them wrong before they try.

npcs.name: Pixie Brightcog
npcs.greeting: The Cartel and the Venture Co. aren't friends, whatever the tauren think. They're ruining a perfectly good forest and a perfectly good reputation for goblins.

npcs.name: Apothecary Merrow Vane
npcs.greeting: The tauren don't want me here, and I understand that. But something in Mulgore is getting the dead back on their feet, and that's my field.

npcs.name: Dr. Hannah Lindqvist
npcs.greeting: I studied volcanoes in Washington State before all this. The one up there looks exactly like one I worked on, and it shouldn't be here at all.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Kauwa
npcs.greeting: There's a bed, a fire and a hot meal. It's crowded, so if somebody's asleep in your bed, wake them gently.

npcs.name: Tal Windstrider
npcs.greeting: The wind riders fly anywhere you've been. They don't like the air over the Blowdown, with all that ash in it, so it's a bumpy ride.

npcs.name: Trainer Mesa Proudhorn
npcs.greeting: I've trained every kind of fighter and caster that's come up this rock. Tell me what you are and I'll show you what's next.

npcs.name: Forgemaster Brak Ironhoof
npcs.greeting: I teach mining and the forge together, and gems if you've got the patience. There's good iron in the Blowdown now that the trees aren't sitting on it.

npcs.name: Tanner Ohanzee
npcs.greeting: Skinning, leather, cloth and cooking, all from the same kill. Pay once and I'll teach you the lot.

npcs.name: Herbalist Nawa Greenmane
npcs.greeting: Herbs and alchemy. Fireweed's the first thing to grow back after a burn, and it turns out it's good for more than looking pretty.

npcs.name: Woodwright Kesh Highfeather
npcs.greeting: Woodcutting and woodworking. I won't teach you to fell the standing giants. Fallen wood's fair; the living trees aren't.

npcs.name: Mistwalker Iyana Rainsong
npcs.greeting: We walk the fog so the giants don't have to stand alone. Keep your voice down near the old ones. Some of them are awake.

npcs.name: Tamsin Reyes
npcs.greeting: I climbed redwoods for a living back in Humboldt County. These ones are bigger than anything we had, and I've never been happier to be wrong about a tree.

npcs.name: Nozzle Quickspan
npcs.greeting: I ran a saw crew for the Venture Co. for six years. I quit the day they started on the living giants. The Cartel took me in, and I've been making it up to the trees ever since.

npcs.name: Alchemist Rennick Toll
npcs.greeting: Undercity sent me for sulphur and ash. The mountain has plenty of both. I'm also told I'm not welcome by the fire, so I stand over here.

npcs.greeting: Bids, buyouts, the whole Horde's junk drawer. Step up, step up. The house takes five percent and none of the blame.

npcs.name: Auctioneer Fazzle
npcs.greeting: Steamwheedle rules, honey. Everybody trades, nobody fights, and the house takes fifteen percent off the top.

npcs.name: Auctioneer Snork
npcs.greeting: Whatever you've got, somebody wants it. Whatever you want, somebody's overcharging for it. Welcome to the block.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Mirabel Sump sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Auctioneer Kizzle
npcs.greeting: Neutral ground, neutral prices, very much not neutral cut. What are we selling?

npcs.name: High Executor Marla Venn
npcs.greeting: This wall is the last thing between the Plaguelands and Tirisfal. Everything east of it wants to come west, and none of it is getting through while I'm standing.

npcs.name: Apothecary Dorian Vesk
npcs.greeting: The Scourge brew their plague in cauldrons out in the fields. I want to know what's in them, and I'd much rather you brought me a sample than a story.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Sabine Holt
npcs.greeting: The beds are hard and the stew is grey, but the door locks, and out here that's the part that matters.

npcs.name: Bat Handler Tobias Crane
npcs.greeting: The bats fly anywhere you've been. They don't like Andorhal, so if you're going there, you're walking.

npcs.name: Deathstalker Ilsa Rook
npcs.greeting: There's an old way under the city that comes out near here. The Royal Apothecaries want it open again, and they want it quietly.

npcs.name: Flamekeeper Rory Callahan
npcs.greeting: I wore the red for a year. I was born in Cork and I laid steel in Boston, and when the world ended the Crusade were the only ones killing what was killing us. Then I saw what else they were killing, so I scraped the red off and walked out. We hunt the mindless dead here, and nobody else.

npcs.name: Priya Raman
npcs.greeting: I ran a guesthouse in Kochi before all this, and I kept the inn on Sorrow Hill. The Forsaken have the beds here, so I've got the Order's kitchen, and nobody goes hungry.

npcs.name: Anders Holm
npcs.greeting: The hawks came down off Sorrow Hill with me. They carry the Order's letters now, not passengers. If you want to fly, the Forsaken's bats are by the west gate.

npcs.name: Drillmaster Kofi Mensah
npcs.greeting: Half my recruits came out of the Crusade and the other half came off the road. The first half can fight, and the second half can think, and I'm trying to get both out of everyone.

npcs.name: Chaplain Odile Marchand
npcs.greeting: I kept Uther's Tomb while we were on Sorrow Hill. Now I keep a chapel behind a Forsaken wall, and the book of names, and I still walk out to the tomb when I can.

npcs.name: Watch Captain Lena Fischer
npcs.greeting: Hearthglen's gate is up the road. They can see us from the walls, and we can see them, and so far everyone's decided that's close enough.

npcs.name: Scout Mateo Brandt
npcs.greeting: Patrols leave the gate at dawn and come back at dusk, and the inquisitors walk the fields in between. If you're going up there, go in the afternoon.

npcs.name: Field Medic Noah Kowal
npcs.greeting: I was a nurse in Winnipeg. Out here I patch up whoever makes it back down the hill, and I don't ask which side they came from.

npcs.name: Captain Joss Varden
npcs.greeting: Crown Guard's been knocked down twice and put back up twice, and it's standing empty now that we're in here. Somebody still has to keep the road to Stratholme open, and that's us.

npcs.name: Greta Lowe
npcs.greeting: I kept the beds at Crown Guard. Jessa's got the beds here, so I've got the kitchen, and nobody's complained yet. Mostly because they're eating.

npcs.name: Gwen Pike
npcs.greeting: I flew Crown Guard's bats. Aldous has the perch here, so I look after the ones that come in hurt. If you want to fly, he's the one to ask.

npcs.name: Commander Eligor Dawnbringer
npcs.greeting: We don't ask where you came from. We ask whether you'll stand on the wall tonight, and most people say yes.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Jessa Moonfield
npcs.greeting: The chapel's ground is holy and the dead won't cross it. You'll sleep better here than anywhere else in the east.

npcs.name: Flight Master Aldous Grey
npcs.greeting: The bats know every road you've walked. I'd fly over Stratholme rather than past it, if I were you.

npcs.name: Archmage Lysander Hale
npcs.greeting: The Scourge carry shards of the necromancy that moves them. Bring me the stones and the Dawn will remember who brought them.

npcs.name: Deathguard Captain Ludo Vance
npcs.greeting: My patrols walk the fields between here and Andorhal. Fewer of them come back every week, and the ones who do are tired of being the only thing out there with a mind.

npcs.name: Surgeon Halbert Grey
npcs.greeting: I stitch the Deathguard back together when the fields take bits off them. It's slow work, and it'd be faster if anything out there were clean enough to use.

npcs.name: Scout Agata Wrobel
npcs.greeting: I was a mountain guide in the Tatras before the Integration. Then I spent a week in a cell under the Scarlet Monastery. I'm back on my feet now, and I'm not going back in a cell.

npcs.name: Ser Aldren Holt
npcs.greeting: I held Andorhal for the King, and then I held it for the Crusade. I walked out with Rory when they started burning people for being born somewhere else. I'm a Lordaeron man, and the people here have told me where they came from. I believe them.

npcs.name: Corporal Ines Duarte
npcs.greeting: I keep the chapel's water clean, which out here means I keep everyone alive. I ran water treatment in Lisbon before the Integration. It's the same job, it's just missing the pipes.

npcs.name: Outrider Bram Tolliver
npcs.greeting: I ride the road west to the river and back, every day. Somebody has to, and the horse doesn't seem to mind.

npcs.name: Edda Marris
npcs.greeting: My husband's family farm is out west, at the stead. They're all still there. I come up here so I don't have to watch them.

npcs.name: Dr. Sun Li
npcs.greeting: I studied fungi in Kunming for twenty years, and I thought I'd seen everything a mushroom could do. The vale out west has taught me otherwise.

npcs.name: Gravewarden Osric Vey
npcs.greeting: The Dawn buries its own, and anyone else who needs it. Terrordale's full of people nobody buried, and I mean to change that.

npcs.name: Lightwarden Ysolde Carrow
npcs.greeting: We pray for the dead here, all of them, because nobody else in the east will. Sit a while, if you need to.

npcs.name: Sergeant Marisol Reyes
npcs.greeting: I was a paramedic in Monterrey. Now I run the chapel's infirmary, and I've got more patients than beds. If you're bleeding, sit down. If you're not, can you carry something?

npcs.name: Ranger Faelis Dawnreach
npcs.greeting: I served at Quel'Lithien Lodge, in the north. Everyone I served with is still there, and none of them are resting.

npcs.name: Ser Roland Ashcombe
npcs.greeting: I was a knight of Lordaeron before Stratholme fell. Now I watch the city for the Dawn, and I try not to recognise the faces at the gate.

npcs.name: Huntress Kaia Lindgren
npcs.greeting: I herded reindeer outside Tromso before all this. The hunting's worse here, and so's the weather, oddly enough.

npcs.name: Pamela Redpath
npcs.greeting: Have you seen my daddy? He went to fight the bad men and he hasn't come home yet. I'm being ever so good while he's gone.

npcs.name: Sister Amalie Crane
npcs.greeting: I was a priestess in Hearthglen. I stood in the room while they questioned the newcomers, and then I walked out. I think I'm still walking.

npcs.name: Woodwright Jonah Lind
npcs.greeting: I built houses in Duluth before the Integration. Now I build palisades, and I'd build them faster if anyone would let me near Hearthglen's timber.

npcs.name: Oona Byrne
npcs.greeting: I fish the river for the Watch's supper. I fished out of Galway for thirty years, and this is the first river that's ever tried to eat me.

npcs.name: Clerk Wendel Ashby
npcs.greeting: I kept Hearthglen's books until I read what I was writing down, and then I left. I still keep books, because it's an old habit.

npcs.name: Flamewarden Teodor Novak
npcs.greeting: I lodge over the tavern and I watch the road east. I was a firefighter in Brno before the Integration, and now I watch a monastery full of people who set fires for a living. The Order of the Pale Flame can always use someone who walks into a burning building on purpose.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Sabine Holt sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Jessa Moonfield sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Beatriz Couto
npcs.greeting: I ran a cafe in Porto, by the river. This is the last bed before Hearthglen, and the walls are thin, so if you snore, the Crusade will hear you.

npcs.name: Roostkeeper Liam Doherty
npcs.greeting: The hawks go anywhere you've been. They won't fly over Hearthglen, and I've stopped asking them to.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Beatriz Couto sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Wyvern-Keeper Rixa Dunlow
npcs.greeting:
Her name's Tolls. Rullo paid for her and he named her, and the name's the part he got right.

She'll take you to Steamwheedle or anywhere else you've been. She won't fly over the holes. I've stopped asking her to, and I've stopped thinking she's wrong.

npcs.name: Gate-Warden Pik Tallow
npcs.greeting:
The gate's for the crawlers, not for you. Come in, and knock the sand off your boots.

We had a camp for three years and nobody needed a gate. Then we built walls, and now somebody has to stand at the hole in them. That's me.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Cook Marda Pell sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Runner Pip Calder
npcs.greeting: I run Captain Varden's letters. I used to run them up the road from Crown Guard, and now I run them across the square, which is a lot less exciting and a lot more alive.

npcs.name: Brother Anselm Hart
npcs.greeting: I keep the chapel's books and write the Commander's letters. He tells me what he means, and I take out the parts that would start a war.

npcs.name: Stablemaster Hob Kettering
npcs.greeting: I kept Crown Guard's horses, and I've still got the ones that lived. I bought most of them from a man I'd now very much like dead.

npcs.name: Ruth Calloway
npcs.greeting: I dug coal in the Rhondda for twenty years before the Integration. The Dawn heard I knew mines and asked me to look at one. I wish they hadn't.

npcs.name: Squire Tomas Wren
npcs.greeting: I carry Ser Roland's shield and polish his boots. He says that's how he started, and he was a knight of Lordaeron, so I'm not complaining.

npcs.name: Pieter Vos
npcs.greeting: Faulk's inquisitors kept me in Hearthglen for a month, asking which Scourge lord I served. I drove a tram in Rotterdam. They didn't know what a tram was, and they took that as a yes.

npcs.name: Pia Lind
npcs.greeting: I'm Jonah's apprentice and his daughter, in that order when he's working. He won't ask anyone for help, so I've started asking for him.

npcs.name: Cipher-Clerk Avery Lusk
npcs.greeting: Loremaster Sennarath sent me down from the Undercity to copy every mark the cult leaves in Pyrewood. Brand lets me sit by his fire, as long as I keep the door shut.

npcs.name: Apprentice Nell Coombe
npcs.greeting: I was one of Haskell's apprentices at the mill. There aren't many of us left, and he's got the rest of us sorting nails so we don't go near the tower.

npcs.name: Old Wenna
npcs.greeting: I've lived on Fenris longer than anyone left in this village, alive or dead. I know the island's old stories, and I've started to wish I didn't.

npcs.name: Deathguard Halsey
npcs.greeting: The Rear Guard sent me to Fenris to write down what's happening here. They don't believe a word of my reports yet, so I've started asking for proof.

npcs.name: Deathguard Mira Holloway
npcs.greeting: I hold the mouth of the cave for Boneward Calder. He goes down to study the bones, and I go down to break them.

npcs.name: Sentinel Ilthara Vale
npcs.greeting: Maestra keeps the post and I keep its wards. The carved posts at the corners are mine, and so is the fishing party, when the lake lets us fish.

npcs.name: Grove Singer Ilyara Moonbrook
npcs.greeting: I sing to the grove, and for as long as I've been singing, it's sung back. Pennarin keeps the Moonwell, and I keep the voices round it.

npcs.name: Seer Tamaka Windmane
npcs.greeting: Dorn asked Thunder Bluff for someone who can read what the Kolkar read. He watches the plain, and I watch the sky over it.

npcs.name: Assayer Brindle Tock
npcs.greeting: I assay ore for the claim, and I read the rig gauges when Nix lets me near them. Everything out here is either worth something or trying to kill you, and my job is telling you which.

npcs.name: Nyx Gearloose
npcs.greeting: Fizzwick and I found the Sinkhole Crater together. He'll tell you he found it alone, and he'll tell you I'm his former partner. The second part's true.

npcs.name: Lookout Shalara Nightbreeze
npcs.greeting: Taelanor and I split the watch on the wall. She watches the sea and I watch the temple mouth, and lately mine's the busier job.

npcs.name: Elder Haldor Mossmane
npcs.greeting: Welcome to the Hold. I sat in the tunnel for three years seeing to Felwood myself, and now the tunnel's open, I can see to it from home. We let the Deadwood leave us, and we mean to bring back whoever of them can still be brought.

npcs.name: Windtalker Selva Brightpelt
npcs.greeting: The passage past my spring goes on to Moonglade again. The druids up there dug it out from their side, them and the strange humans they call the Wakened, and now the wind brings the glade down to me as well as Felwood's drums.

npcs.name: Pathfinder Grosk
npcs.greeting: I walk the tunnel down to Felwood every morning and count what's changed in Felpaw. Every morning, something has.

npcs.name: Featherkeeper Imna
npcs.greeting: Every Deadwood wears the headdress, and every headdress was a Timbermaw's once. Bring me their feathers and I'll see they're burned properly.

npcs.name: Honeykeeper Tova
npcs.greeting: The honey comes down from the Hold's hives in these crates. Every bear in Felwood can smell it from the tunnel mouth, and every one of them has tried.

npcs.name: Warden Bramblecoat
npcs.greeting: Come in, then. The Elders opened the tunnel to anyone who comes in peace, and you've come in peace or you'd be lying at the bottom of the hill.

npcs.name: Warden Durn Rockpelt
npcs.greeting: This passage went on to Winterspring, once. The day the world changed, the roof came down, and nobody's dug far enough to say what's on the other side.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Layla Saleh
npcs.greeting: My brother and I had a guesthouse in Aqaba, on the Red Sea, and most of our guests were divers. Now it's orcs who snore and elves who complain about them, and it's the same job. He's the one who dreams. I'm the one who keeps the books.

npcs.name: Windrider Master Kragga
npcs.greeting: The wyverns go anywhere you've already been. They don't like the coast, because something big moves out past the spires at night, and I don't make them fly over it.

npcs.name: Grunt Mazkar
npcs.greeting: Orc on this side of the gate, elf on that side. We take turns being the one who's right.

npcs.name: Spellbreaker Ilanthe
npcs.greeting: I watch the road for satyrs. The grunt watches the road for satyrs. Neither of us watches the other, officially.

npcs.name: Overseer Durgash Stonejaw
npcs.greeting: Orgrimmar sent me to keep the dig honest. Everything that comes up out of the ground gets counted twice, once by me and once by the elves, and the counts never match.

npcs.name: Grand Magister Velanthe Sunreach
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Firstlight Spire. We lost the spires of Quel'Thalas, and the Conclave swore we'd raise a light again somewhere. Here it is, and it's yours as much as ours.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Bortha Mossbelly
npcs.greeting: There's a bed by the fire and honey bread in the morning. Outsiders sleep at the inn, and nobody minds what you are so long as you keep your boots off the furs.

npcs.name: Totemkeeper Ungar Ashbrow
npcs.greeting: Every bear on the great totem was an Elder of the Hold. The carvers add one when an Elder dies, and they haven't had to add one for the Deadwood yet. I'd like to keep it that way.

npcs.name: Springwarden Lessa Brightwater
npcs.greeting: The spring comes up from under the mountain, clean, the way it always has. Since the deep gate started to stain, I taste it every morning before anyone drinks.

npcs.name: Deepwarden Grothar
npcs.greeting: The deep gate stays shut. Whatever turned the Deadwood came up from under the Hold, and the Elders sealed it the night they found out. Don't stand on the crack.

npcs.name: Deepwarden Ulma
npcs.greeting: We take turns listening at the gate. Some nights it's quiet, and some nights something on the other side is digging.

npcs.name: Carver Bennik Ashpaw
npcs.greeting: That totem in the yard has been waiting for its last face for a year. The Elders haven't decided whose it should be, and I'm not carving a face for somebody who isn't dead.

npcs.name: Ingrid Solberg
npcs.greeting: I was a park ranger in Jotunheimen before the Integration. The Timbermaw took me in when the Horde camps wouldn't, and now I keep the long hall's stores. Bears that talk back took some getting used to.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Hrolm
npcs.greeting: The pass down to Azshara's forest is steep, and the satyrs watch the bottom of it. Come and go in daylight if you can.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Tibba
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Timbermaw Hold. Mind the Elders, mind the hives, and don't go near the gate in the floor.

npcs.name: Tunnelwarden Burrfoot
npcs.greeting: The tunnel's through there, all the way to Felwood. It's a long walk in the dark, so take a torch and follow the totems.

npcs.name: MerchantTusk
npcs.greeting: Dere is only one bank, mon, and dere is only one me. Do not ask how dat works. Hand me ya things and go be a hero.

npcs.name: Auctioneer Fizzbit Coppercrank
npcs.greeting: The Timbermaw don't haggle, they trade, and they write down every deal. Put it on the block and the whole Horde can bid. The house takes its cut, same as anywhere.

npcs.name: Envoy Grashak Stonetusk
npcs.greeting: Orgrimmar sent me to keep the road to the Hold open. The Elders let me sit on their terrace and wait, and I've learned that waiting is most of what an envoy does here.

npcs.name: Trainer Ursa Greymantle
npcs.greeting: I've trained warriors, healers and the odd mage the Elders took in. Tell me what you are and I'll show you what's next.

npcs.name: Forgekeeper Dunn Ironpelt
npcs.greeting: Mining, the forge and gems. The ore's deep in this mountain, and the Hold's been digging it since before your grandparents' grandparents.

npcs.name: Hidewright Tess Softpaw
npcs.greeting: Skinning, leather, cloth and cooking, all from the same kill. Pay once and I'll teach you the lot.

npcs.name: Herbwarden Fenna Mossbrow
npcs.greeting: Herbs and alchemy. The racks dry what the terraces grow, and I don't let any of it go to waste.

npcs.name: Woodwright Brann Oakpaw
npcs.greeting: Woodcutting and woodworking. The carvers take the best wood for the totems, so you'll learn on what's left, same as I did.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The Hold's mailbox, between the bank and the auction house. Innkeeper Bortha sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Mohammed Saleh sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Magister Caelin Brightspire
npcs.greeting: I catalogue everything that comes out of the ground. The orcs catalogue it too, and then we compare lists, and then we argue about the lists.

npcs.name: Magistrix Ysolde Emberwind
npcs.greeting: There's a ward under this courtyard older than Silvermoon, and it's still awake. Mind where you put your feet.

npcs.name: Salvage Boss Rukka Ironhide
npcs.greeting: My crews do the lifting and the elves do the pointing. If you've got arms and you're not afraid of a ghost, I've got work.

npcs.name: Dr. Amara Okafor
npcs.greeting: I dug Iron Age sites in Nigeria for twenty years and I've never seen anything like this. Both sides pay me, and both sides think I'm theirs. I'm the dig's.

npcs.name: Farseer Thrag Windcaller
npcs.greeting: The leylines under this coast are pulling toward the sea. The elves say that's fine. The spirits say it isn't.

npcs.name: Captain Zarga Bloodfang
npcs.greeting: Stormwatch sees the whole coast from here, and I don't like most of what I see. Something came up out of the sea with that city, and it isn't done coming up.

npcs.name: Ranger Thessaly Dawnsong
npcs.greeting: The Conclave sent me to watch the Drowned Court. My grandmother's grandmother walked those streets, and now there's seaweed growing on them.

npcs.name: Grunt Okkar
npcs.greeting: The satyrs burned Valormok a month ago. I'm the last of the watch who didn't leave, and I'm not leaving until somebody pays for it.

npcs.name: Spellwarder Aelis Dawnmere
npcs.greeting: I keep the Conclave's wards on the dig, and lately they've started pointing out to sea. That isn't what wards are supposed to do.

npcs.name: Chief Liquidator Halyna Bondar
npcs.greeting: My father kept his dosimeter on the kitchen shelf in Slavutych, next to the salt. He said it was so he'd remember. I didn't understand what he meant until I came over that last rise and saw the wheel standing in the middle of this pass.

npcs.name: Kenji Watanabe
npcs.greeting: At Fukushima we wrote our names and our readings on a sheet at the end of every shift. Here I write them on the board by the pyre, and the readings are worse and the list of names is shorter. Has anyone checked your dosimeter today?

npcs.name: Deathguard Harrow
npcs.greeting: I used to count the living who came through this gate and the dead who didn't come back. I stopped when the second number caught up with the first. Scrub at the troughs, and then you can go wherever you like.

npcs.name: Old Tobiah
npcs.greeting: Anything that dies too near the wheel gets up again unless it's burned, so I burn it, and I talk to it while it goes because somebody ought to. Mind the smoke. It burns green for a reason.

npcs.name: Dr. Aigerim Seitkali
npcs.greeting: I grew up in Semey, beside the Polygon, where the Soviets tested their bombs for forty years and told nobody downwind. Half my patients were born with those tests in their blood. I came here because I know what this looks like long before anyone admits it.

npcs.name: Master Apothecary Morwen Ashgrave
npcs.greeting: The Seep barely troubles the dead, which makes my people the only ones who can walk out there for long. The Undercity wants to know what it is. So do I, for reasons of my own, and you'll find I pay very well for samples.

npcs.name: Apothecary Lisbeth Vane
npcs.greeting: Master Ashgrave writes down everything the Seep does. I write down everything Master Ashgrave does. Somebody in the Undercity reads both, and I'd like it to be the right somebody.

npcs.name: Luiz Ferreira
npcs.greeting: In Goiania in 1987, two scrap men opened an old hospital machine and found a powder inside that glowed blue in the dark. People took it home because it was beautiful. My uncle rubbed it on his arms at a party. So when somebody here picks up a piece of glowing glass and smiles at it, I take it off them.

npcs.name: Rine Lajuon
npcs.greeting: My grandmother was a girl on Rongelap in 1954, when ash from the Bravo test came down like snow and the children played in it. They moved our people off the island, then back, then off again. I build the things that keep people away from places now, and the spire is the biggest one I've ever built.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Sela Crowe
npcs.greeting: Every town keeps a fire and a bed, even this one. The living sleep badly here and the dead don't sleep at all, so I'm up either way. I'll bind your hearth here if you want it.

npcs.name: Bat Handler Ossian Reed
npcs.greeting: The bats won't fly over the middle of the pass. Something about the wheel turns their ears inside out, and I've stopped trying to make them. I'll take you anywhere else they know.

npcs.name: Corporal Ray Delgado
npcs.greeting: Welcome to the fence. My grandmother grew up in St. George, Utah, downwind of the Nevada tests, and the government told her those clouds were nothing to worry about. So I never tell anybody anything's nothing to worry about. Scrub at the Watch before you hug anyone.

npcs.name: Agatha Morgan
npcs.greeting: This was my family's ground long before anybody called it a plot. I was buried in it once, in that crypt there, and I dug my own way out. Now the ground keeps changing its mind about what it holds.

npcs.name: Grull the Younger
npcs.greeting: The little one in me remembers when the clan used to sing. The big one remembers what the clan did after the singing stopped. Both of us want it finished.

npcs.name: Ariden
npcs.greeting: I've watched that tower every evening for forty years, and every evening the light in the high window goes out at the same moment. It's this evening again, isn't it? It's always this evening.

npcs.name: The Bridge Echo
npcs.greeting: ...I can see the far side from here. Halya, tell them the readings are wrong. Tell them it isn't a hole at all, it's a...

npcs.name: Baba Hanna
npcs.greeting: They moved us out of Kupuvate in 1986 and told us three days. I walked back in the next spring with my sister, and I stayed thirty years. A pass full of ghosts doesn't frighten me. I've buried worse than ghosts.

npcs.name: Deathstalker Vessa Morrow
npcs.greeting: The Dark Lady wants eyes on the middle of the pass, and the living don't last out here. I don't have that problem. The things out there are older and younger than they should be, sometimes both at once.

npcs.name: Rabine Saturna
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Nighthaven. The Circle has kept this glade for ten thousand years, and it still looks the way it always has, which is exactly what worries me. Something here is waking, and I'd like to know what before it opens its eyes.

npcs.name: Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem
npcs.greeting: I led what was left of Thunder Bluff's druids up the mountain to this glade. We carried the ones who couldn't walk, and we left the ones we couldn't carry. Moonglade took us in, and I won't forget it.

npcs.name: Bunthen Plainswind
npcs.greeting: The wind riders and the hippogryphs share a roost now, and they've mostly stopped biting each other. I flew the Thunder Bluff road every day for twenty years, and I still fly it most nights in my sleep. Where can I take you?

npcs.name: Innkeeper Talowyn Nightbreeze
npcs.greeting: Every bed in Nighthaven faces the lake, so you'll fall asleep to the moon on the water. I'll bind your hearth here if you want to come back to it.

npcs.name: Trainer Loganaar
npcs.greeting: The Circle trains druids, and lately it trains everyone else too, because everyone else keeps arriving. Tell me what you are and I'll show you what's next.

npcs.name: Herbwarden Mylla Starbloom
npcs.greeting: Herbs and alchemy. Nothing grows in this glade that the Circle hasn't tended, so I'll teach you here and you'll gather out in the world.

npcs.name: Hidewright Tannar Proudhoof
npcs.greeting: Skinning and leather. My people wasted nothing from a kill on the plains, and I won't have you wasting anything here either.

npcs.name: Ilyssa Moonwater
npcs.greeting: Cooking and fishing. The lake's fish have never once been hungry enough to bite in a hurry, so you'll learn patience before you learn anything else.

npcs.name: Moonwell Keeper Aedris Silverbrook
npcs.greeting: The great moonwell has never run dry, not in ten thousand years. Lately it runs over at night, a finger's width, and then it settles again by morning. I've started writing down when.

npcs.name: Elder Mahala Dawnhorn
npcs.greeting: We brought the totems out of Thunder Bluff on our backs, and we haven't raised them yet. Raising them here would mean we'd stopped hoping to go home.

npcs.name: Keeper Remulos
npcs.greeting: I've walked the Dream since before your world's first city was built. Lately the Dream has been turning over inside me, the way a sleeper does before he wakes. I'm not afraid of it, and I'm listening hard.

npcs.name: Dreamwatcher Lethiel
npcs.greeting: The stones of this arch are warm at night. They were cold for ten thousand years, and now they're warm, and nobody in the Circle will tell me why. So I sit with them.

npcs.name: Warden Taerenas
npcs.greeting: The Barrow Dens are closed. The sleepers inside have started talking in their sleep, and the Circle wants nobody listening at the door until we know who they're talking to.

npcs.name: Warden Torin Grayhoof
npcs.greeting: I stand here so the sleepers aren't alone. I knew some of them on the plains. One of them still owes me a game of stones, and I mean to collect.

npcs.name: Dr. Ingrid Sandvik
npcs.greeting: I studied sleep in Trondheim for twenty years, what the brain does at night and why it dreams. Then I woke up on the grass beside that lake with a druid standing over me, and I've been studying it from the inside ever since. Welcome to the Wakened.

npcs.name: Nurse Adaeze Okafor
npcs.greeting: I was a night nurse in Lagos. When I woke up here I went looking for the sick before I'd even asked where I was. Some of us wake badly, and I sit with them until they're sure which world they're in.

npcs.name: Hamish MacLeod
npcs.greeting: The first thing I remembered when I woke was my mother's kitchen on Lewis, so I carved it into a plank. Now everybody carves the last thing they remember, and the wall's longer than the longhouse.

npcs.name: Mei-Lin Zhou
npcs.greeting: My grandmother grew chillies on a balcony in Chengdu. The druids say nothing here needs my help to grow, and they're right, but I plant things anyway. It's how I know where I am.

npcs.name: Danny Kowalczyk
npcs.greeting: I had a wife and two boys in Buffalo, and I was asleep when it happened. If I fall asleep the right way, I think I'll wake up back there. Ingrid says it doesn't work like that. I keep trying anyway.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Sela Crowe sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Talowyn Nightbreeze sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Greul
npcs.greeting: There are more bedrolls than beds now, but there's a fire and a roof for everyone. I'll bind your hearth here if you want to come back to us.

npcs.name: Wind Rider Master Shyn
npcs.greeting: The wind riders carried half the camp out of the Needles on their backs. They'll carry you anywhere you've already been.

npcs.name: Brave Takoda Mistrunner
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Mojache. Keep your weapons sheathed inside the totems, and don't ask the new arrivals where they came from. If they want to tell you, they will.

npcs.name: Chieftain Ahanu Swiftstrider
npcs.greeting: When the first of them walked in out of the Needles, half starved, I didn't count them. I just opened the gate. Mojache is twice what it was, and I'd do it again.

npcs.name: Hadoken Swiftstrider
npcs.greeting: My sister runs the camp and I keep it fed. The forest gives plenty, if the gnolls and the Grimtotem would leave us enough of it to hunt.

npcs.name: Elder Nayeli Cloudhoof
npcs.greeting: I walked out of Mulgore with forty others and a cart of totems. Thirty-one of us got here. I say the names of the other nine every night, so the forest learns them too.

npcs.name: Krueg Skullsplitter
npcs.greeting: Orgrimmar keeps an eye on this camp, and I'm the eye. Mostly I watch the ogres at Dire Maul's gate, and lately they've been watching back.

npcs.name: Trainer Ishana Brightmane
npcs.greeting: Whatever you came here as, I can teach you the next of it. The camp needs everyone at their best, and that includes you.

npcs.name: Brann Tallgrass
npcs.greeting: I keep the list. Everyone who walked in, where they came from, who they're looking for. It's a long list, and the part with the names crossed off is getting longer.

npcs.name: Hidewright Onawa Redcloud
npcs.greeting: Skinning and leather. Nothing that dies in this forest goes to waste in this camp, not while there are people sleeping under bare poles.

npcs.name: Herbalist Kele Windsong
npcs.greeting: Herbs and alchemy. The forest here grows things I'd never seen in Mulgore, and a few I'd never seen anywhere, from where the strange trees came in.

npcs.name: Sentinel Aelyra Tidewatch
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Feathermoon. Transplants may land, and plenty have. Keep to the paths and speak to the General if you're looking for work.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Shyria
npcs.greeting: The inn's small and the walls are thick, and nobody's ever been cold in here. I'll bind your hearth to the island if you'd like.

npcs.name: Shandris Feathermoon
npcs.greeting: I've held this island through wars that would have ended your world twice over. The sea has been restless since the merge, and so has the coast. If you're here to help, there's work.

npcs.name: Latronicus Moonspear
npcs.greeting: I keep the record of the Highborne ruins on this coast, what's standing and what's been taken. Lately the second list grows faster than I can write it.

npcs.name: Sentinel Selarin
npcs.greeting: I watch the coast from here to Sardor Isle. The Hatecrest come up the beaches at night now, and they don't come to raid. They come to dig.

npcs.name: Kindal Moonweaver
npcs.greeting: There's a forest on the coast that wasn't there three years ago. The trees are older than they should be, and they don't answer when I speak to them. The people living under them do.

npcs.name: Huntress Jalara Nightwind
npcs.greeting: The chimaeras on the Isle of Dread have started going for the boats. A chimaera doesn't change its hunting ground without a reason, and I'd like to know what it is.

npcs.name: Trainer Nalia Moonbrow
npcs.greeting: The Sentinels train every sister on this island, and the General says we train you too. Tell me what you are and I'll show you what's next.

npcs.name: Herbalist Taelan Greenleaf
npcs.greeting: Herbs and alchemy. The coast grows lotus and sungrass for anyone patient enough to look, and the Sentinels go through healing draughts faster than I can brew them.

npcs.name: Fisherwoman Elyssa Gullwind
npcs.greeting: Cooking and fishing. The nightfin run off this island every evening, and if you can't catch one here, you can't catch one anywhere.

npcs.name: Fyldren Moonfeather
npcs.greeting: The hippogryphs fly the coast and inland as far as you've been. They don't fly over the Isle of Dread, and neither would you if you'd seen what nests there.

npcs.name: Scout Wapi Longstride
npcs.greeting: You came down off the mountain? So did half my camp. Camp Mojache is just west of here, inside the totems. Tell them Wapi sent you.

npcs.name: June Nakamura
npcs.greeting: I was a ranger in Olympic National Park for sixteen years. I know every one of these trees by name, and none of them should be on this continent.

npcs.name: Walt Hollis
npcs.greeting: I logged out of Forks for thirty years. Then I woke up under the same trees on the other side of the world, and I haven't cut a single one. Felt like I owed them that.

npcs.name: Rosa Ibarra
npcs.greeting: I was an ER nurse in Tacoma. Out here I'm the only nurse, and the closest thing to a pharmacy is whatever grows by the creek. So I've learned what grows by the creek.

npcs.name: Sam Okonkwo
npcs.greeting: I studied fungus at Portland State. The mushrooms in these groves came with the trees, and some of them are spreading into the old forest. Nobody here knows what that means yet, including me.

npcs.name: Sentinel Mirael Duskbrook
npcs.greeting: The boats leave for Feathermoon from this pier. Step aboard if the General's expecting you, or if you want her to be.

npcs.name: Sentinel Aerwyn Starbrook
npcs.greeting: This is the Sentinels' Watch, as far north as Feathermoon reaches. From here we can see the Colossals, Ravenwind and the Bough, and lately none of them are quiet.

npcs.name: Tahu Swiftrunner
npcs.greeting: Mojache sent me north after the Rage Scar. The yetis have come down out of their hold, and a yeti doesn't leave its hold for nothing.

npcs.name: Dreamwatcher Sylanna
npcs.greeting: The Circle sent me from Moonglade. The stones there are warm at night, and so are this tree's roots. I'd like to know whether it's the same warmth.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Greul sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The inn's mailbox. Innkeeper Shyria sorts the letters, parcels and whatever the auction house owes you.

npcs.name: Orwin Gizzmick
npcs.greeting: I came out here to buy silithid resin, because it sells. Then I found out where it comes from, and now I'm the one asking adventurers to go and look. Business has its days.

npcs.name: Headwoman Zula Rootcaller
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Rootwater, where the tree drinks the sea. The High Chieftain sits up in the Settlement, and down here at the roots it's me. If you're going up, I'll want your help first.

npcs.name: Witch Doctor Tazjin
npcs.greeting: The loa of this tree never had a name before we gave it one. It answered us when nothing else did, and I listen for it every night. Lately it's been hungry.

npcs.name: Huntress Ka'lisa
npcs.greeting: Everything that drinks the sap grows. The crocolisks in the lagoons are twice the size they were last year, and they've stopped being afraid of us.

npcs.name: Fizzle Brasswinch
npcs.greeting: I built every lift on this tree, and the trolls paid me in sap. Best deal I ever made, until the Bloodsail figured out what it's worth.

npcs.name: Sapwatcher Uzo
npcs.greeting: The sap is the tree's blood. A little heals a cut, a cup makes a man strong, and a barrel makes a beast into something else. I measure it, so somebody has to.

npcs.name: Marta Kowalczyk
npcs.greeting: I came over on the Zoram boat to see the tree everyone was talking about, and I never got back on. The trolls let me stay if I work, so I work.

npcs.name: Boatman Grik'zul
npcs.greeting: Grom'gol's across the water, a short pull with a good tide. Step in when you're ready and keep your hands inside, the crocolisks have gotten bold.

npcs.name: Boatwoman Zaela
npcs.greeting: This boat goes all the way across to Zoram Strand, on the night elves' coast. It's a long row, and the Sentinels there have gotten used to trolls turning up.

npcs.name: Scout Jinzo
npcs.greeting: I watch the lagoons for the Rootmaw. It's the oldest croc on the island, and it's been drinking from the roots since the first day. Don't swim out there alone.

npcs.name: Elder Tal'vani
npcs.greeting: Mossroof was the first village we built on the tree, before anybody dreamed of a city in its heart. The young ones go up, and I stay here, where the boughs are wide and the falls are short.

npcs.name: Bough-Hunter Rakaz
npcs.greeting: The apes on the west bough have been drinking the sap, and the spiders on the east have been eating the apes. I hunt both, and I never run on a branch I haven't walked first.

npcs.name: Rivercaller Jinda
npcs.greeting: A river shouldn't run along a branch, but this one does, and it's never once run dry. I listen to it. Lately it's been saying the Bloodscalp are climbing again.

npcs.name: Bridgekeeper Ozzu
npcs.greeting: Every rope and every plank between the boughs is mine to keep. If a bridge sways, that's the wind. If it creaks, come and tell me.

npcs.name: Scholar Vel'jani
npcs.greeting: The scholars in the Settlement pay good silver for sky-bones, the bronze and crystal pieces that fall out of the clouds and catch in the branches. I'm here to buy every one I can find.

npcs.name: Aroha Tane
npcs.greeting: I climbed trees for a living back home, big kauri in the north of New Zealand. Then I heard about this one. I came up for the view, and I'm still here.

npcs.name: Stairwarden Mozu
npcs.greeting: The Root Stair goes all the way down to the landing on Rootwater, and every step of it's been worn smooth by somebody's feet. Mind the bottom ones, they're wet.

npcs.name: Liftkeeper Grizzik
npcs.greeting: Fizzle down at the landing built the little lifts. I built this one, and it goes all the way up to the Settlement. Step on when you're ready and keep your elbows in.

npcs.name: Scout Halaja
npcs.greeting: I watch the Howling Bough from here. The apes used to throw fruit at us. Now they throw each other, and the big silverback with the gold tooth throws anything he likes.

npcs.name: Scout Tiko'ra
npcs.greeting: The Bloodscalp come up the ropes at the end of the Great Bough. I've cut their ropes twice this month, and they've tied new ones twice.

npcs.name: High Chieftain Zan'kaji
npcs.greeting: The tree answered us when the world broke. We climbed it, and we'll keep it. Help us and you're one of the tribes, whatever you were born.

npcs.name: Loa-Speaker Vashi
npcs.greeting: This temple is the loa's ear. Every tribe that climbed the tree left something at its feet, and the tree remembers every one of them.

npcs.name: Envoy Grukk Ironjaw
npcs.greeting: Orgrimmar sent me to ask the High Chieftain to call the tree Horde ground. He gave me a room, a view and a very long wait. I'm starting to like the view.

npcs.name: Liftwarden Ozenna
npcs.greeting: The Great Lift goes down to Mossroof and the Lower Boughs. Grizzik built it and I keep it, which means I'm the one he shouts at when it squeaks.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Krosh'ta
npcs.greeting: Welcome to the Great Settlement. Keep your weapons sheathed, keep to the bridges, and don't lean over the rails, it's a long way down to Mossroof.

npcs.name: Liftwarden Tagu
npcs.greeting: The High Lift goes on up to the Middle Boughs, where the old shrines are. The air's colder up there, and the bark isn't as healthy as it ought to be.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Ma'kali
npcs.greeting: Beds upstairs, stew down here, and the best view in the tree from the back balcony. Rest a while and I'll mark you as one of mine.

npcs.name: MerchantTusk
npcs.greeting: Dere is only one bank, mon, and dere is only one me, even way up in a tree. Do not ask how dat works. Hand me ya things and go be a hero.

npcs.name: Auctioneer Kezzik Boltbelly
npcs.greeting: Put it on the block and the whole Horde can bid, even from down on the ground. The house takes its cut, the lift takes its cut, and you get what's left.

npcs.name: Scholar Yenvaa
npcs.greeting: Every piece on this wall fell out of the clouds. Bronze, crystal, gears finer than any goblin makes. Somebody up there's losing a great deal of something.

npcs.name: Kofi Mensah
npcs.greeting: I ran a stall at Makola Market in Accra, back home, before the merge. A market's a market, whether the customers have tusks or not. These ones haggle better.

npcs.name: Hana Sato
npcs.greeting: My family kept a tea house in Kyoto for four generations. The trolls had never had green tea until I came. Now half the Settlement starts the day here.

npcs.name: Trainer Zal'jin
npcs.greeting: Warrior, healer, hunter or something stranger, the tribes take everybody. Tell me what you are and I'll show you what comes next.

npcs.name: Forgehand Bok'ra
npcs.greeting: Mining and the forge. The ore comes up from the stones caught in the boughs, and I teach you to find it and to make it into something.

npcs.name: Tinkerer Sprazzle
npcs.greeting: Gems and gadgets, jewelcrafting and engineering. The sky keeps dropping parts on us, and somebody has to learn what to do with them.

npcs.name: Hidewright Sen'jo
npcs.greeting: Skinning and leatherworking. Python skin, ape hide and the odd spider's carapace, it all comes through my hands before it goes on somebody's back.

npcs.name: Brewer Ya'tali
npcs.greeting: Herbalism and alchemy. Half of what grows on the tree doesn't grow anywhere else, and the other half grows faster here than it should.

npcs.name: Weaver Mazala
npcs.greeting: Tailoring and enchanting. The silk from the Silkwood takes an enchantment better than any cloth I've ever worked.

npcs.name: Carver Hekta
npcs.greeting: Woodcutting and woodworking. We never cut the living tree, only what it drops, and it drops a great deal.

npcs.name: Cook Tum'bo
npcs.greeting: Cooking and fishing. The falls pool has fish nobody can name, and every one of them is good in a stew.

npcs.name: Grandmother Ozai
npcs.greeting: I was the first to sleep in this ward, when it was three huts and a rope. Now look at it. The young ones don't remember the jungle, and I'm glad.

npcs.name: Lamplighter Jinto
npcs.greeting: I light every lantern in the ward at dusk, and I've never missed one. Grandmother Ozai says if one goes out, the loa can't find its way home.

npcs.name: Weaver Kesha
npcs.greeting: The streamers on the Rise are mine, every one, and so are half the awnings in the market. Red for the tribes, teal for the tree, gold for the loa.

npcs.name: Bat Handler Ruzkah
npcs.greeting: The bats fly down to Grom'gol and out across the Horde's roads. They don't like the dark under the tree, so they fly fast, and you'll want to hold on.

npcs.name: Archivist Tel'zan
npcs.greeting: The scholars' hall keeps a record of everything that's fallen from the sky. The record gets longer every week, and the pieces get bigger.

npcs.name: Watersinger Ya'nela
npcs.greeting: The water falls from a branch so high nobody's climbed to it. It's never stopped, not once, and it tastes a little sweet, like sap.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The Settlement's mailbox, between the bank and the auction hall. Innkeeper Ma'kali sorts the letters, the parcels and whatever the auction hall owes you.

npcs.name: Gardener Ula'ni
npcs.greeting: Everything the ward eats that isn't fish grows on this terrace. The soil came up the lift a basket at a time, and the tree's sap makes it give twice what it would on the ground.

npcs.name: Shadow Hunter Vokra
npcs.greeting: Heartwatch watches one thing, and it's the split in the trunk behind me. Something down in the heartwood is eating this tree, and until we know what, nobody goes in and nothing comes out.

npcs.name: Loa-Speaker Ganjo
npcs.greeting: I listen to the tree for the tribes. It used to sing. Now it groans at night, low and long, the way a sick man does when he thinks nobody's listening.

npcs.name: Bark-Doctor Ezzi
npcs.greeting: The rot starts as a soft spot you can push your thumb into, and a month later you can push your whole arm in. I cut it out where I can. I can't cut out a whole bough.

npcs.name: Huntmaster Raz'gul
npcs.greeting: The harpies came up from the coast when the world broke and found the hollows in the bark. They've been fattening on the rot's grubs ever since, and they've got bold.

npcs.name: Stonekeeper Jo'than
npcs.greeting: The first climbers built these terraces, stone carried up a tree, block by block. Nobody remembers how. I keep them swept and I keep their names, and that's my whole job.

npcs.name: Scholar Nyara
npcs.greeting: Tel'zan sent me up from the Settlement after the thing on the Lichen Reach. It fell out of the clouds a month ago and it hasn't stopped moving. I'd like to know what it's for before it finishes whatever it's doing.

npcs.name: Dr. Priya Raman
npcs.greeting: I'm a plant pathologist from Bengaluru, and this is the biggest sick patient I've ever had. The rot behaves like a fungus I know from home, except that it's hungry in a way fungi shouldn't be.

npcs.name: Ropehand Dezza
npcs.greeting: Tagu works the bottom of the High Lift and I work the top, and we shout at each other all day. Step on when you're ready to go back down to the city.

npcs.name: Scout Mahu
npcs.greeting: Something out at the end of the Reach fell out of the sky, and it's still twitching. Little metal things keep crawling out of it. I count them every morning, and there's more every day.

npcs.name: Scout Ree'na
npcs.greeting: The harpies roost in the hollows on the south bough, and their matron keeps a nest inside the trunk itself. I've heard her screaming from in there, and it carries all the way to Heartwatch.

npcs.name: Windwarden Kazra'jin
npcs.greeting: Highrest is as far as anyone lives. Above us the branches get too thin to build on, and then there's only cloud. I've climbed into it three times, and three times I came back down.

npcs.name: Wyvern-Tamer Gu'lok
npcs.greeting: The wild wyverns roost on the east boughs, and some of them will take a rider if you're patient and you don't mind losing a finger. I've lost two, and I'm still patient.

npcs.name: Stormcaller Ixi
npcs.greeting: Lightning hits this tree more than anything else in the world, because it's the tallest thing in the world. One bolt split the trunk open and the storm crawled inside. It's still down there, and I can hear it thinking.

npcs.name: Skywatcher Tal'mae
npcs.greeting: A boat fell out of the sky onto the north bough, a boat with no water under it. Tel'zan wants to know who sailed it, and so do I. Its guardians don't want us to know at all.

npcs.name: Old Muzzi
npcs.greeting: I climbed with Ruk'tan and Zel'ji when we were young and stupid. Ruk'tan turned back, and Zel'ji didn't come back. I've got one more climb left in these knees, maybe.

npcs.name: Ingrid Haugen
npcs.greeting: I'm a mountaineer and a meteorologist from Tromso, so I've spent my life where the weather is worst. This tree makes its own. It pulls storms in like a mountain does, and I've never seen anything like it.

npcs.name: Stairwarden Rhoka
npcs.greeting: The root stair goes back down to Heartwatch, and I count everyone who comes up it. I count them going down again too, and the numbers don't always match.

npcs.name: Ladderkeeper Vosh
npcs.greeting: My grandfather hung the last ladder up there, above the cloud. I keep the knots on this end, and I check them every morning, because he'd climb down and kill me if I didn't.

npcs.name: Scout Tazzo
npcs.greeting: The roosts go on further than you'd think, and every one has a wyvern in it. I watch the big one with the crest, because when she flies, the whole flock flies with her.

npcs.name: Scout Neema
npcs.greeting: The wreck's guards don't sleep and they don't eat. I've watched them for nine days. They walk the same circle round the boat, and they've never once stepped off it.

npcs.name: Gatewatcher Zul'mo
npcs.greeting: Everybody who comes up through the old wall stops right where you're standing and stares. Take your time. Then go west to Spearhold, because the war-leader wants every spear he can get.

npcs.name: Old Ranjo
npcs.greeting: Look straight down the Hollow, past the trunk. The green smudge down there, ringed with water, is Stranglethorn, and the village I was born in is somewhere in it. I come out here every morning to make sure it's still there.

npcs.name: War-Leader Rakkuzi
npcs.greeting: The sky people walked onto our tree and called it a meeting. Then their soldiers fell on the meeting, and now they hold the north arm. Zan'kaji sent me up here to throw them off it, and I'm going to, whatever Orgrimmar's envoy has to say about it.

npcs.name: Envoy Garrok Blackmane
npcs.greeting: The Warchief sent me to keep the Horde out of a war it doesn't understand. The trolls want blood, the scholars want to talk, and the soldiers who hit the parley want the whole tree. I'm trying to work out which of them is lying to me, and so far it looks like all three.

npcs.name: Witch Doctor Zanshi
npcs.greeting: There's light coming up through the cloud east of here, where the old stones sink into it. It isn't sunlight, and it gets stronger every time the sky ships fire their guns. The loa won't tell me what it is, and that scares me more than the soldiers do.

npcs.name: Scout Jinra
npcs.greeting: The soldiers dug in across the north arm in a single night. They've got poles that hum and throw up a shield, and guns that throw lightning. I counted their lancers twice, and both times I came back with a bigger number.

npcs.name: Rider Taz'kal
npcs.greeting: My wyverns won't fly anywhere near the beasts on the islets. They've never been scared of anything in their lives, and now they shake in their roosts at night. Something up here is bigger than they are, and they know it.

npcs.name: Ilaren Vey
npcs.greeting: I came down here to talk, and I was halfway through my first sentence when the Ascendancy's ship came down on the stones. They're my own people, and they fired on me without a word. My house says the ground is primitive. I'm starting to think the ground's the only one up here being reasonable.

npcs.name: Speaker Hezza
npcs.greeting: I stood on these stones for the Highbough. The pale one across from me was talking about trade when the sky ship came down, and I saw his face. He was as surprised as I was. The war-leader won't believe that, but I was there and he wasn't.

npcs.name: Archivist Elyon Sarre
npcs.greeting: This ring was old before the first of our cities ever left the ground. The Kharad built it, the giants, and they cut warnings into every stone. I can read about one word in three, and every word I can read means keep it shut.

npcs.name: Leandro Arrieta
npcs.greeting: I was a paragliding instructor in Bariloche, and I woke up on a rock in the sky with my wing in shreds. The scholars found me two weeks later. I've lived with them for three years now. They're good people, mostly, but not one of them has ever asked me if I want to go home.

npcs.name: Dr. Rania Azar
npcs.greeting: I was a doctor in Beirut, and now I'm the only doctor for thirty people on a cloud. The scholars stand behind me while I work and write down everything I do. Yesterday one of them asked me why we bother to set a broken bone. I'm still working out how to answer him.

npcs.name: Pavel Novak
npcs.greeting: The survey wants me to look at their engines, the ones that hold whole cities up in the sky, and they want my opinion. I designed bridges in Brno. I said yes before anyone could change their mind.

npcs.name: Ewan Docherty
npcs.greeting: I climbed that tree from the roots, every branch of it, and I thought I'd be the first one to the top. It turns out there were thirty people already living on a cloud up here, and not one of them had to climb.

npcs.name: Hunter Dak'zin
npcs.greeting: The sky beasts come down to drink where the falls go over. Some of them are the size of a hut and float like they're full of air. I've hunted everything Stranglethorn has, and I still don't know where to put the spear in one of these.

npcs.name: Dockmaster Saren Holt
npcs.greeting: The gangway's open, and Lenswatch is across it. Mind your feet at the far end, because the island drifts a hand's width on its chains and nobody's got round to fixing it.

npcs.name: Scout Muzza
npcs.greeting: This is as close as you get without a shield of your own. Past those humming poles the lancers see you before you see them. I lost two brothers learning that.

npcs.name: Survey Guard Orrin Talvas
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Lenswatch. Keep your weapons sheathed on the stone, and please don't touch the lens. The surveyor will want to meet you, because he wants to meet everyone who comes up.

npcs.name: Keeper Aurel Quan
npcs.greeting: The House built this guesthouse for visitors from the ground, and you're the first ones who've actually slept in it. The beds are soft, the food is strange, and the wind can't get in. If you want to come back here quickly, I'll mark your hearthstone.

npcs.name: Skiffmaster Toren Valdis
npcs.greeting: The skiffs fly down to the troll city and back. They'll go further once the council lets us, but for now the sky past the shelf belongs to the Ascendancy's patrols.

npcs.name: Surveyor-Captain Ilvaro Destren
npcs.greeting: The House of the Patient Lens sent me to study the tree and the people on it. I've spent my whole life measuring things, and I can't measure this. The tree's still growing, the trolls want us gone, and our own soldiers are shooting at my camp. Sit down and tell me what the ground thinks of us.

npcs.name: Lensmaster Coryn Aldaer
npcs.greeting: On a clear day the great lens can see a coin on the ground from up here. I've watched your cities for a year. Your Orgrimmar has very loud markets, and I mean that as a compliment.

npcs.name: Warden Sellis Varn
npcs.greeting: The Earth people are guests of the House. We found them on islands nobody lives on, starving and frightened, and we took them in. Some of them call that a kindness and some of them call it a cage. I'm honestly not sure which of them is right.

npcs.name: Archivist Tavian Rell
npcs.greeting: Everything the survey learns comes through this hall, and we write it all down twice. The Ascendancy took our first copy when they came down on the stones. We think they wanted what we'd learned about the old ring in the cloud.

npcs.name: Shipmaster Corin Haldane
npcs.greeting: She's the oldest hull in the House's fleet, and she's flown further than any of the new ones. She's got one more long flight in her, and the surveyor's saving it for getting everyone home, if it ever comes to that.

npcs.name: A Fallen Piece of the Mural
npcs.greeting: A slab of painted stone from the old wall lies face up in the moss, and a little of the golden sun is still on it.

npcs.name: Ilaren Vey
npcs.greeting: The wards were Kharad. They woke when the seal cracked, and they fired on the first Aetherian ship they saw, which was ours. Aurelion's that way, up the river. We'll walk it, then.

npcs.name: Leandro Arrieta
npcs.greeting: Three years in the sky and I've never once been in a crash. I've been in a lot of falls, but a crash is different. Help me get these people up the river, and I'll owe you a drink in Aurelion.

npcs.name: Skiff-Pilot Varo Senn
npcs.greeting: Something on the islands below lit up and the skiff's crystal went dark in my hands. I put her down where I could. I'm sorry it wasn't softer, and I'm sorry my leg won't hold me yet.

npcs.name: Herald Cassian Orel
npcs.greeting: The council sent me to bring you to Aurelion with all the courtesy of the High Houses. The courtesy is somewhere in that wreck. The invitation still stands, if you'll walk it.

npcs.name: Landing Hand Hask Merrow
npcs.greeting: The survey's skiff comes and goes from here to Lenswatch, and it flies low and slow now that the old stones shoot at anything bright. Mind the gangway, it's newer than the rest of us.

npcs.name: Elder Merek Vale
npcs.greeting: I come here to watch the river go over the edge. It's gone over for as long as I've lived, but lately I've started counting the islands that go over with it.

npcs.name: Scholar Idris Marrowell
npcs.greeting: The House of Long Memory says the Kharad were here before we were, and the rest of the houses laughed at us for it. Then their war-golems stood up. Nobody's laughing now, and I've never been so frightened to be right.

npcs.name: Kaisa Lehtonen
