npcs.greeting: I ran search and rescue out of Rovaniemi, so I'm good at finding people who don't want to be lost. Thirty-one of us woke up on these rocks. We're still finding the last few.

npcs.name: Gustavo Pires
npcs.greeting: I did rope access on the towers in Rio, hanging off the side of a building with a bucket. Tying two rocks together over the sky is the same job, it's just a much longer fall.

npcs.name: Annelies de Vries
npcs.greeting: I grew tomatoes under glass outside Westland, forty hectares of them. I had a packet of seeds in my coat when I woke up here, and the first one came up blue. I'm still deciding if I'd eat it.

npcs.name: Dr. Ana Kealoha
npcs.greeting: I spent fifteen years counting humpbacks off Maui, and I thought I'd seen every kind of big animal there was. Then one swam past me through a cloud. I've been out here every day since.

npcs.name: Keeper Ithren Lorrow
npcs.greeting: Halcyon Rest has stood on this river since before Aurelion had its outer rings. We feed whoever comes down the water, and lately that's mostly people whose homes fell.

npcs.name: Skiffmaster Davin Sorell
npcs.greeting: The skiffs still fly, low and dark, with the crystals hooded so the old stones don't see us. I'll take you down to the tree's city or across to Lenswatch, but not higher, not yet.

npcs.name: Teodric Ashlane
npcs.greeting: I lived on the Eighth Ring of Aurelion, the outermost, the one that fell. I was at the market when it went, and so I lived. My street didn't.

npcs.name: Dace Morrow
npcs.greeting: I was a sky lancer until they told us to fire on a parley. I put my lance down on the stones and walked. Don't thank me for it. I should have put it down years ago.

npcs.name: Aqueduct-Warden Lorne Ishay
npcs.greeting: That's Aurelion's water coming down, through what's left of the Fourth Aqueduct. It's meant to turn back into the city. Instead it spills, and the whole Expanse drinks it.

npcs.name: Bridgewarden Caldus Rhee
npcs.greeting: The sky-bridge is Aurelion's door, and it stays shut until the council sends word. I know they invited you. I've also seen what's come up that bridge lately, so I'll wait for word.

npcs.name: Armwarden Teska Rell
npcs.greeting: The arm's carried water and walkers between the shelf and the Spillway for longer than Aurelion's had its rings. It's never carried a ground-walker before, but it'll carry you. Mind the cracks.

npcs.name: Steward Olin Varrow
npcs.greeting: House Vaelith has held this estate for eleven hundred years. The family went to Aurelion when the shelf began to lean, and I stayed with the house, because somebody has to wind the clocks.

npcs.name: Corwen Vaelith
npcs.greeting: My grandmother's grandmother planted that orchard. Everyone else left for the city, and I couldn't. If the shelf goes, I'd rather be standing on it than reading about it.

npcs.name: Warden-Prime Aldric Sorne
npcs.greeting: The Anchor-Wardens have kept these three anchors for a thousand years, and we've lost an island once. Look south-west at the Dropfield and you'll see what that looks like. I don't mean to see it twice.

npcs.name: Chainwright Hollis Venn
npcs.greeting: Every link in the First Anchor's chains has a name and a wright who forged it. Most of them died before my great-grandfather was born, and the links still hold. The Third Anchor's don't.

npcs.name: Engineer Pell Oravane
npcs.greeting: I read the anchors the way a healer reads a pulse. The First is steady, the Second's in the Ascendancy's hands so I can't read it at all, and the Third's been slipping for forty years. It's slipping faster now.

npcs.name: Scout Varen Ashby
npcs.greeting: The Ascendancy took the Second Anchor and said they'd hold it better than we could. They don't know the first thing about it, and every day they hold it, it drifts a little more.

npcs.name: Old Warden Ebbe Tharn
npcs.greeting: My grandfather's grandfather saw the island fall, the one that's the Dropfield now. He told it to his son, and it came down to me the same way, word for word. I'd rather not add a new ending.

npcs.name: Skiffmaster Jorun Kell
npcs.greeting: The skiffs fly from Keelstone to Halcyon Rest and down the tree. Not over the Second Anchor, though. The Ascendancy shoots at anything that isn't theirs.

npcs.name: Master of Measures Ivo Kestrel
npcs.greeting: The House of Measures has written down the shelf's lean every night for a thousand years. For most of those years the number barely moved. I'm the first master who's had to buy a bigger ledger.

npcs.name: Star-Reader Caelan Duir
npcs.greeting: The stars don't move, so when an island moves against them, I see it. The Listing Isle has moved more this year than in the last two hundred.

npcs.name: Archivist Bram Iselworth
npcs.greeting: Our oldest records are older than the anchors, and they're in a hand nobody in the house can read any more. We copy them anyway. You don't throw away a book because you can't read it.

npcs.name: Margit Halvorsen
npcs.greeting: I kept oil rigs standing in the North Sea for twenty years, so a leaning island doesn't scare me much. What scares me is that the people who built it have stopped understanding how it works.

npcs.name: Bartosz Wierzbicki
npcs.greeting: I was a land surveyor in Krakow, and the first thing I did up here was measure the tilt. It's four degrees and climbing. I measure it every morning, because somebody ought to.

npcs.name: Dr. Ngozi Eze
npcs.greeting: I was a doctor in Ibadan, and now I treat sprained ankles on a slope and chest pains from the Aetherians who climb over to tell us we're camped in the wrong place.

npcs.name: Engine-Tender Halvard Cree
npcs.greeting: These engines have fed the anchors since before the houses had names. I know every one of them by the sound it makes. Lately they're making sounds I don't know.

npcs.name: Warden Siran Holt
npcs.greeting: I'm posted at the Third Anchor to watch it slip, and to go down to the keel if anyone ever finds the nerve. The last wardens who went down never came back up.

npcs.name: Wade Prentiss
npcs.greeting: I salvaged wrecks off Halifax for a living. A whole island fell here a few hundred years ago, and nobody's ever properly picked it over. That's the best wreck I've ever been on.

npcs.name: Gatewarden Tessa Vell
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Aurelion. The rings are older than any house in the city, so walk them gently, keep to the bridges, and don't lean over the rails. The fall goes on longer than you'd like.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Sela Arro
npcs.greeting: The Arro guesthouse has kept rooms on the Bridgefoot for four hundred years, and we've never had a ground-walker sleep in one. Rest here, and I'll mark you as one of ours.

npcs.name: MerchantTusk
npcs.greeting: Dere is only one bank, mon, and dere is only one me, even way up in de sky. Do not ask how dat works. Hand me ya things and go be a hero.

npcs.name: Auctioneer Mira Dorne
npcs.greeting: The Exchange has set the price of crystal for a thousand years. Put your goods on the block and the whole Horde can bid from the ground. The council takes its share, as it always has.

npcs.name: Skiffmaster Elian Vos
npcs.greeting: The skiffs fly from the Bridgefoot to every island the city still trades with, and down the tree to the ground. They're the oldest service in Aurelion, older than the Exchange.

npcs.name: Herald Odric Fane
npcs.greeting: Every proclamation of the council for nine hundred years was first read from this plaza. The one that opened the gates to the ground was the shortest in the record.

npcs.name: Ilaren Vey
npcs.greeting: We made it, and by the long way round, which my house will say was always the proper way. Stand here a moment and look at it. I've lived here all my life and I still stop on this plaza.

npcs.name: Leandro Arrieta
npcs.greeting: Three years I heard about this place, and they never let us past Lenswatch. Now I'm standing in it and the herald just bowed to me. My mother in Buenos Aires would never believe a word.

npcs.name: Keeper of the Spire Ulmar Seyth
npcs.greeting: The Spire is the city's first stone. The rings were built round it, one by one, over a thousand years. The keepers have tended it all that time, and we still don't know who raised it.

npcs.name: First Speaker Aldren Sorvaine
npcs.greeting: The council has argued about the ground for a hundred years. Then the seal cracked, and an argument became a door. You're the first to walk through it, and the houses are watching to see what we let in.

npcs.name: Councillor Thalos Wren
npcs.greeting: I speak for the House of the Patient Lens, the house that sent the survey down your tree. Half the council called it a waste of crystal. They're quieter this season.

npcs.name: Councillor Idrel Marrowell
npcs.greeting: The House of Long Memory has always said there was more to the sky's past than the other houses like to teach. My granddaughter found it standing up on the Golem Fields.

npcs.name: Master of the Academy Halvric Oune
npcs.greeting: The Academy has taught every magister in Aurelion for eight centuries. This year it has students asking whether the ground has scholars, and nobody on the faculty knows the answer.

npcs.name: Gardener Tamsin Ashgrove
npcs.greeting: The Gardens were planted when the Inner Ring was laid, and some of these trees are older than the Academy. Walk the lawns, but please don't pick the gold apples, because every one of them is counted.

npcs.name: Ambassador Tavia Morrane
npcs.greeting: The council opened this hall for the ground the week the seal cracked. It's the newest building in Aurelion by about three hundred years, and you can still smell the mortar.

npcs.name: Hamid Sadeghi
npcs.greeting: I was an interpreter in Tehran for twenty years, and now I interpret for the Ground Embassy. The Aetherians have eleven words for respect and none of them mean quite the same thing.

npcs.name: Dockmaster Garret Lune
npcs.greeting: The great airships put in here, the long-haulers that cross the whole sky. Fewer of them every year, and none at all from some of the old routes.

npcs.name: Warden of the North Gate Orsk Talmar
npcs.greeting: The north gate opens on the road to the low country, the islands where the young ones learn the sky. It's quiet out there, and the road is long.

npcs.name: Elder Corrin Ashlane
npcs.greeting: The Eighth Ring fell in my lifetime. We were the outermost ring for nine hundred years, and then we weren't. My nephew Teodric walked down the river to Halcyon Rest. I stayed here, with what's left of us.

npcs.name: Mother Ysolde Marsh
npcs.greeting: The council sends bread and the houses send coin, and the Eighth's Rest makes soup out of both. Nobody here goes hungry, even if nobody here goes home.

npcs.name: Trainer Kestrin Dorrow
npcs.greeting: The Trainers' Ring has taught every discipline the sky knows, and now it'll teach the ground's. Tell me what you are, and I'll show you what comes next.

npcs.name: Forgewright Brannoc Dray
npcs.greeting: Mining and the forge. Sky-ore runs through the rings' stone, and I'll teach you to find it and to make it into something that deserves the name.

npcs.name: Crystalwright Amma Fesk
npcs.greeting: Jewelcrafting and engineering, which up here are nearly the same trade. Everything in this city that moves, moves on crystal.

npcs.name: Tanner Rusk Odell
npcs.greeting: Skinning and leatherworking. Sky-beast hide is lighter than anything on the ground and tougher than you'd guess.

npcs.name: Herbalist Lioren Paske
npcs.greeting: Herbalism and alchemy. The Gardens' herbs have been grown for the Academy's alchemists for eight hundred years, and they're very particular about who picks them.

npcs.name: Weaver Sennet Clay
npcs.greeting: Tailoring and enchanting. Aetherian cloth takes an enchantment the way still water takes light.

npcs.name: Woodwright Garan Hesk
npcs.greeting: Woodcutting and woodworking. Wood is rare in the sky, so every plank in Aurelion has a history, and I can tell you most of them.

npcs.name: Cook Hamar Quill
npcs.greeting: Cooking and fishing. The Gardens' pool has fish that were brought up from the islands six hundred years ago, and they've been very well fed since.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: Aurelion's mail pylon, between the inn, the bank and the Exchange. Innkeeper Sela Arro sorts the letters, the parcels and whatever the Exchange owes you.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The survey's mail pylon by the guesthouse. Keeper Aurel Quan sorts what comes up the tree and what goes down it.

npcs.name: Captain Isolde Marrane
npcs.greeting: I was ordered to fire on Tethertown, a camp of Earthborn who'd done nothing but be there. I brought my ship down here instead, with everyone aboard who agreed with me. She'll never fly again, and I've never been prouder of her.

npcs.name: Magister Orla Thessan
npcs.greeting: I taught Maelis Ardane everything she knows about the sky. She was the brightest student the Patient Lens ever had, and she decided we were too slow. I came here to watch what she's building, because I think I owe the sky that much.

npcs.name: Lancer Tavin Roake
npcs.greeting: I put my lance down at the Proving Grounds in front of my whole wing. Half of them laughed, and three of them followed me here that night. I'd like to get the rest out before the warships sail.

npcs.name: Surgeon Nell Avary
npcs.greeting: Most of what I treat is burns from the storm guns, and the rest is what the Proving Grounds does to young lancers. The Ascendancy calls that training. I call it a waste of good people.

npcs.name: Skiffmaster Pell Daray
npcs.greeting: The free skiffs land at the wreck and nowhere nearer the fort, because the Gunline shoots at anything it doesn't recognise. I can get you to Aurelion or anywhere else that's still friendly.

npcs.name: Lookout Fen Arden
npcs.greeting: From the bow I can see the whole quay. They've laid three new keels this month, and the yard works through the night now. Whatever they're building it for, they're in a hurry.

npcs.name: Rosa Delgado
npcs.greeting: I welded pipelines in Monterrey for fifteen years. The Ascendancy found that out, and now I weld warships. I'm very good at it, and I'm very careful about which seams I make strong.

npcs.name: Siobhan Keane
npcs.greeting: I was a ward nurse in Galway. Here I've got two hundred patients, one tent and whatever the deserters can smuggle in. Ask me how they're doing and I'll tell you the truth.

npcs.name: Tomasz Bielecki
npcs.greeting: My father made sails in Gdansk, and so did I. The warships take sails of a kind I've never seen, but cloth is cloth and a knot is a knot. I remember every ship I've rigged here, every one.

npcs.name: Clerk Anselm Rook
npcs.greeting: My job is to read what the Inquisitors bring me and burn what they tell me to burn. I copy everything first. I'm not brave, but I can't watch a thousand years go into a brazier.

npcs.name: Storm-Keeper Edda Quill
npcs.greeting: I kept these collectors for the old house that owned this rock, before the Ascendancy came. They kept me on because nobody else knows how to make the storm behave. Neither do I, most days.

npcs.name: Hamza Qureshi
npcs.greeting: I had a curry house in Bradford with forty covers. Now I feed two hundred people on what the yard throws out, and nobody's sent a plate back yet.

npcs.name: Warden Kael Ostry
npcs.greeting: I count everyone who comes up the road, and I've counted three columns of soldiers this week and one of you. I'll admit I'm gladder to see you than I was to see them.

npcs.name: Keeper Sabine Aldour
npcs.greeting: This is the last shrine on the Firmament that's still lit. As long as it burns, the people here have a reason to stay, and I'll keep it burning as long as they do.

npcs.name: Magistrate Ilse Varrow
npcs.greeting: I was magistrate of the Firmament when it had nine towns. Now it has one camp, and I'm still magistrate, because somebody has to say what happens to the people who stayed.

npcs.name: Magister Orla Thessan
npcs.greeting: I followed Maelis north. She's here, at the Moorage, with the fleet that's meant to take the tree. I taught her to read the sky, and now I've got to watch what she's doing with it.

npcs.name: Skiffmaster Dorran Vale
npcs.greeting: Mine's the last skiff that still flies out of the Firmament. I can get you to the Bastions, to Aurelion or anywhere else that's still friendly.

npcs.name: Cutter Ansel Fennick
npcs.greeting: I cut the crystals for the shrine. I'm the last crystal-cutter on the Firmament, and I've got nothing left to cut but what you bring me.

npcs.name: Sipho Ndlovu
npcs.greeting: I ran a scrapyard in Durban for twenty years. Up here the islands drop scrap on you every day, and the Aetherians pay me to tell them which bits still work.

npcs.name: Annika Sjoberg
npcs.greeting: I taught primary school in Umea before the change. There are eleven children in this camp, and somebody has to teach them their letters while the world falls apart round them.

npcs.name: Archivist Theodora Quell
npcs.greeting: The House of Long Memory has said for a thousand years that the Kharad were here before us, and the other houses have laughed at us for a thousand years. The Threefold Forge is why I'm not laughing back.

npcs.name: Scholar Rhun Adaire
npcs.greeting: I read Kharad runes, which makes me the only person at Forgewatch who can tell you what the giants' hearth says. Mostly it tells you to mind your feet.

npcs.name: Kwabena Osei
npcs.greeting: I shod horses and mended ploughs in Kumasi. The Archivist brought me up here to tell her how a forge works, and this one has three hearths, which no forge I ever saw had.

npcs.name: Lens-Warden Corra Hale
npcs.greeting: The Ascendancy's salvage crews come past the camp every day to get into the Hearthdeep. They haven't come into the camp yet, and I'd like to keep it that way.

npcs.name: Old Benedek Saar
npcs.greeting: Everyone else on this street left forty years ago, and the rest of the Quarter went after them. I was born in that house, and I'll go when it does.

npcs.name: Gardener Yllen Moss
npcs.greeting: Every garden on this island went grey but this one tree. I come out every morning to see if it's still green, and so far it always has been.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Ivo Darrance
npcs.greeting: I fed the Ascendancy's army for twenty years. I've seen what the general means to do with it, and I've stopped wanting to be the one who feeds it.

npcs.name: Maud Saltpenny
npcs.greeting: You came out past the last island on purpose? Then you're either a fool or a beachcomber, and I'm both. Sit down before the gulls see you.

npcs.name: Durek Ashfoot
npcs.greeting: Nobody walks in here by accident. I didn't. I came for the glass and the glass kept me. Don't touch anything that's still glowing.

npcs.name: Koji'ra
npcs.greeting: You found the way out here. Then the isles let you. They don't let many.

npcs.name: Fizzle Brassgut
npcs.greeting: Shh! Keep your voice down, the gods are napping. Probably. Want to get rich?

npcs.name: Rizzo Dustwhistle
npcs.greeting: My great-great-grandmother's caravan is under this sand somewhere. So's her money.

npcs.name: Brannoc Dustmane
npcs.greeting: I climbed down to see where the ground went. Now I'm the only one who knows.

npcs.name: Ithrael Nightwell
npcs.greeting: My grandmother sealed this place. I came to find out why. Speak quietly.

npcs.name: Halvard Grey
npcs.greeting: Lightning hits the same place twice up here. Four times, sometimes. Don't stand near the stones.

npcs.name: Marta Hollis
npcs.greeting: This was my family's orchard. It still is, I suppose. Mind the apples.

npcs.name: Grandmother Ash'ka
npcs.greeting: You found my granddaughter's tree. Good. She was always going to send someone. Sit, child. Listen to the roots.

npcs.name: The Librarian
npcs.greeting: Shh. Not because of the books. Because of what's reading them.

npcs.name: Walt Dempsey
npcs.greeting: Stay on the white ground, off the colours. The colours mean the crust's thin, and under the crust it's boiling.

npcs.name: Vesna Orlova
npcs.greeting: Breathe slowly. There's more air down here than you're built for, and it goes to your head before you notice.

npcs.name: Ilsabet Graves
npcs.greeting: Keep your voice down. The water listens, and when it hears a living voice it starts to cry.

npcs.name: Sami Halonen
npcs.greeting: Walk where the moss is grey, not where it's green. Green moss floats. I spent twenty years in the bogs outside Oulu and this one still scares me.

npcs.name: Dr. Ana Vukovic
npcs.greeting: Keep your voice down and your hands where the mammoths can see them. They're not used to people. Nobody's been here for twenty thousand years.

npcs.name: Lirael Brightwater
npcs.greeting: You came through the ward? Then it's weaker than I thought. Stay on the road, keep out of the light at the north end, and don't go near the Magister.

npcs.name: Old Ma'luu
npcs.greeting: Mind the moss at the edge, it's softer than it looks and the water's deeper than you'd think. I came up here to pray for rain when I was young. Look how that turned out.

npcs.name: Dr. Luana Ferreira
npcs.greeting: Keep your voice down, the howlers are deciding whether they like you. I studied this canopy for twelve years from a tower outside Manaus, and one morning the whole thing was somewhere else, and so was I.

npcs.name: Kelsey Draper
npcs.greeting: Keep low when you cross the quill, the birds take anything that stands up tall. I chased storms out of Norman, Oklahoma for nine years, and I've never once seen one sit still.

npcs.name: Tessaly Ombrine
npcs.greeting: You found it too? Then don't tell the House, please. I've measured every ring in this place twice, and I'm not ready to share it with anyone.

npcs.name: Ressa Vane
npcs.greeting: If the Bastions sent you, you can tell them I'm dead. It's nearly true. If they didn't, mind the soft cloud and don't touch anything with a crest on it.

npcs.name: Mireya Lanz
npcs.greeting: Welcome to the top of the world. I led groups up here from Santa Elena for twenty years, and it was always the top of the world. It's just that now there's nothing underneath it.

npcs.name: Ranger-Captain Saelis Dawnbrook
npcs.greeting: Take it easy, you're all right. You're on Dawnhaven, an island off the coast of Azshara, and you're safe. Everyone wakes up on this shore confused. Sit until the sand stops moving.

npcs.name: Magistrix Iriel Brightleaf
npcs.greeting: The wardstones kept this island hidden for a thousand years. Now they're broken, and things are finding us. I mean to mend them, one stone at a time.

npcs.name: Apothecary Thaelen
npcs.greeting: Sit down if you're dizzy. The first day here does that to everyone. I've got tea for the shaking, and something stronger for the dreams.

npcs.name: Rosa Quintero
npcs.greeting: I built houses in Valparaiso for twenty-two years, on hills worse than this one. The elves know magic. I know roofs, and right now the roofs are winning.

npcs.name: Scout Kaelen Swiftarrow
npcs.greeting: There are naga on the south-east beach, and they weren't there a month ago. Keep your voice down near the cove.

npcs.name: Priestess Aldaria Morningsong
npcs.greeting: The outpost buried its own at the Silent Barrow, up the north-west road, and they don't sleep the way they should. I keep their names here, and some nights they come asking for them.

npcs.name: Trainer Aelwyn Starsong
npcs.greeting: Every one of the disciplines came through Amberwatch at one time or another, and I've taught them all. Tell me which is yours, and we'll begin.

npcs.name: Herbalist Mireth
npcs.greeting: Peacebloom in the grove, silverleaf by the mere, earthroot wherever the ground's been turned. That's where to start, and I'll show you how.

npcs.name: Prospector Daelan
npcs.greeting: Copper in the stones at the wardstones, and there's more under the barrow, if you don't mind the company. I'll teach you to dig it out.

npcs.name: Tanner Ysolde
npcs.greeting: Every boar and lynx on this island is a hide somebody needs. Learn to take it cleanly, and Rosa will pay you in roofing.

npcs.name: Lightwarden Selanne Dawnsworn
npcs.greeting: The Lightwell fed this whole outpost once, and it's dark now. Light it again, and Dawnhaven stops being a ruin we're hiding in. It becomes a home.

npcs.name: Magister Aeron Ashveil
npcs.greeting: The outpost's magic didn't die when the well went dark. It spilled out into the woods. Some of it has woken up in the thicket, and it's hungry.

npcs.name: Huntress Lyra Swiftbough
npcs.greeting: The Red Hollow feeds us, if you hunt it properly. Something's made the bears bold this year, and the spiders bolder.

npcs.name: Commander Halion Brightspear
npcs.greeting: You can stand easy here. I held this outpost when it fell, and I've held it every day since. I'm not sure there's much of me left to hold it with.

npcs.name: Scout Nerys Duskmantle
npcs.greeting: Keep your head down. That's the naga's main camp below us, and they've got sentries on the rocks. I've been counting them for three days.

npcs.name: Spire-Keeper Lorien Ashbloom
npcs.greeting: The founders raised this spire and lit it, and it burned for a thousand years. When it went out, the outpost died with it. I've kept the stair swept ever since, waiting.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Liriel Ambershade
npcs.greeting: A bed, a fire and a hot meal, and nobody asks where you washed up from. That's the whole of the Spire's hospitality, and it's more than most of us had a year ago.

npcs.name: Hawkmaster Seraphel
npcs.greeting: The dragonhawks will take you anywhere you've already been. They'll cross the strait to Azshara on a calm day, and they think the boat is beneath them.

npcs.name: MerchantTusk
npcs.greeting: Dere is only one bank, mon, and dere is only one me, even out here on de elves' island. Do not ask how dat works. Hand me ya things.

npcs.name: Mailbox
npcs.greeting: The Spire's mailbox. The innkeeper sorts the letters and the parcels, and the boat brings the rest from Durotar.

npcs.name: Trainer Elthas Dawnreach
npcs.greeting: The library keeps every discipline's books, and I keep the library. Show me how far you've come and we'll see how far you can go.

npcs.name: Smith Torvael
npcs.greeting: The Spire's forge is small, but the anvil came from Silvermoon. Bring me ore and I'll teach you the hammer, or the pick if you'd rather.

npcs.name: Alchemist Sylvana Brightdew
npcs.greeting: Mana potions, healing draughts, and a tea that stops the dreams. Learn the herbs first, then the glass.

npcs.name: Tailor Marelle
npcs.greeting: Red and gold, always. Everyone who comes ashore needs clothes that fit this place, and I need hands. Sit down and I'll show you the needle.

npcs.name: Enchanter Vaelis
npcs.greeting: Every scrap of old magic on this island wants to go somewhere. Enchanting gives it somewhere to go.

npcs.name: Joost Achterberg
npcs.greeting: Forty years I brought ships into Rotterdam, the biggest port in Europe. Now I've got one boat and one crossing, and I'm prouder of it than I ever was of the big ones.

npcs.name: Dockhand Grezza
npcs.greeting: The elves' boat comes in from Dawnhaven every few days. Orgrimmar's up the road to the north, and Razor Hill's south-west of here. Mind the scorpids.

npcs.name: Maren Eide
npcs.greeting: I was on a night bus outside Bergen, and then I was here, wet to the knees. The elves keep telling me that's normal. I don't think it's normal.

npcs.name: Tomasz Wrobel
npcs.greeting: The ranger told me to sit until the sand stops moving. It's been an hour, and it's still moving a little.

npcs.name: Sentinel Daeron Highwind
npcs.greeting: Amberwatch keeps its gate open from dawn to dusk. After dark it opens for anyone the shore gives up, and for nobody the sea sends.

npcs.name: Sentinel Taelia Brightshore
npcs.greeting: I watch the cove road. If you hear horns from the south-east, it's the naga, and you'd best be inside the walls before the second one.

npcs.name: Caelan Ashgrove
npcs.greeting: I carried this bundle out of Quel'Thalas, across the sea and up this hill. I keep meaning to unpack it. I'll get round to it when there's a roof to unpack it under.

npcs.name: Taelor Brightwood
npcs.greeting: Rosa doesn't speak a word of Thalassian, and I'd never held a saw until this week. We understand each other perfectly. She points, and I cut.

npcs.name: Guard Valandor Emberleaf
npcs.greeting: Dawnrest had no roof for a thousand years, and it's got one now. I'd rather nothing came down the road to test it.

npcs.name: Mirelle Oakensong
npcs.greeting: We put the roof back on with timber from the Red Hollow. It leaks over the hearth, which means it leaks over the cook, which means I hear about it every night.

npcs.name: Hunter Belathor Thornleaf
npcs.greeting: Lyra takes the bears, and I take whatever she leaves. The stew's been good since you lot started thinning the woods.

npcs.name: Andrés Calderón
npcs.greeting: I drove a lorry in Seville. Now I carry water for the elves, and honestly, the pay's about the same. The view's a great deal better.

npcs.name: Spire Guard Lethandris
npcs.greeting: Welcome to Firstlight Spire. Keep to the road, mind the stair, and don't stare at the light too long. Everyone does on their first night.

npcs.name: Spire Guard Caerwyn Dawnfeather
npcs.greeting: The boat crosses when Joost says the sea's fit, and not before. Arguing with him doesn't help. I've watched a magister try.

npcs.name: Lady Elandris Vael
npcs.greeting: I had a house in Silvermoon with forty windows. Here I've got one room with a single window, and the spire's in it. I find I don't miss the other thirty-nine.

npcs.name: Faeril Lightquill
npcs.greeting: The library has more books than shelves, so we read them standing. I've got three on runes and one on boats, in case the runes don't work out.

npcs.name: Haldris Netweaver
npcs.greeting: The fish here bite at dusk and sulk at noon, the same as the fishermen. Sit a while if you like. They don't mind company.

npcs.name: Siobhan Reilly
npcs.greeting: I came ashore half drowned in the spring. Now I've got a room over the bakery and a cat who belongs to nobody. That's more of a home than I had in Galway, if I'm honest.
